item.title: Horrified witnesses recount fatal rollercoaster incident at Six Flags
item.description:
Theme park company Six Flags temporarily closed nine rollercoasters across six amusement parks on Monday after one person died and several others were injured in an incident involving a coaster in Georgia. Officials did not confirm how the person died, nor how the others were injured or their conditions. Witnesses who spoke to NBC affiliate WXIA of Atlanta said they saw a man fall from the Goliath rollercoaster. “He fell and hit the car three different times,” one witness told the station. Death on Six Flags rollercoaster in US triggers ride closures across six states Continue reading...

Sources: BBC News, CBS News, The Guardian

item.title: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack
item.description:
Bulgaria has seen the second spate of drone attacks on merchant ships off its coast in the past week. Russia has been accused of repeatedly targeting civilian cargo ships in the area.

item.title: Spanish royals visit Ceuta amid tensions with Morocco over migrant influx
item.description:
Spain’s King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia visited Ceuta for the first time in 14 years on Tuesday, as the North African enclave grapples with the aftermath of a mass migrant influx. Authorities have cleared makeshift camps from the beaches ahead of the visit, amid strained relations with neighbouring Morocco.

Covered by 3 public.
Sources: Al Jazeera English, Deutsche Welle, France 24

item.title: Rwanda to host a Grand Prix in 2030s as Formula One returns to Africa
item.description:
The last time Formula 1 hosted a race in Africa was way back in 1993. But a new track in Rwanda is set to host a Grand Prix in "the early 2030s," continuing the country’s investment in international sport.

item.description:

You can read our latest full report here: Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say Some more Gulf reaction to Houthi’s deadly airport attack and continued threats to target Saudi airspace. The UAE message is improtant given the major rupture in relations this year between the two oil-rich kingdoms, first sparked by lingering divisions in Yemen, and made worse by the Iran War and arguments over oil prices which led to the UAE quitting OPEC (currently led by the Saudis) after six decades of membership. item.description:
